name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 30 points, among the bluest in the nation
Raskin holds a roughly 450-to-1 fundraising advantage, with $7.9 million on hand versus about $1,800 for Riley
Nationally prominent incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside opposition spending
No public polling; prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97%
model.rationale: The district's 30-point Democratic lean, Raskin's overwhelming cash advantage over a Republican rival who has raised under $17,000, and market pricing near 97% for Democrats leave no realistic path for an upset; the only real uncertainty is the size of the winning margin.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major scandal or the incumbent's unexpected departure from the race, would put the outcome in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 8th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 30 points. Jamie Raskin, a nationally prominent incumbent, is seeking re-election and holds an enormous financial edge, having raised about $7.4 million and banked $7.9 million. Republican Cheryl Riley has raised under $17,000 and has roughly $1,800 available, leaving her little capacity to run a competitive campaign. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot with no reported fundraising.

No public polls track the race, and prediction markets price Democratic odds near 97%. With no sign of serious outside investment on either side and the district's strong Democratic tilt, the seat sits firmly in the Safe Democratic column. The open question is the size of the margin rather than the winner, with the incumbent positioned to win decisively.
